newsitem.title: INDIA: Shell to start exploration of India block June '98.
newsitem.headline: Shell to start exploration of India block June '98.

text.p: Shell India Development Ltd, a subsidiary Royal Dutch/Shell, will commence exploratory drilling in a northwestern Indian block next June, a company official said on Monday.
The RJ-ON-90/1 block in the state of Rajasthan was put on offer in India's fourth exploration round and a contract with the Indian government was signed in May 1995.

"Preliminary survey of the Barmer-Sanchor block has shown encouraging results. Next year, we will go in for drilling at Gudha village south of Barmer," David Corbishley, chief executive of Shell India Development, told Reuters.
Shell India has so far spent $10 million in conducting a seismic survey of the block and plans to invest an additional $6.0 million in drilling the exploratory well, he said.
Corbishley refused to divulge the forecast reserves in the well but said it was "worth spending the money ($6 million) in evaluating the prospect."
Shell is one of the six firms which have won licences to explore for oil and gas in Rajasthan.
